summary: One Gettysburg take cloned from a synthetic or a human reference, or sampled hotter: the #1386 reference A/B.
description: Reference A/B (#1384 stage A): Audio8-TTS (the voice-clone template's model and call) speaks one passage of the Gettysburg Address, one take of 111 words or fewer, in the voice of 'reference_audio', whose exact words are 'reference_text'. The arms are bench/arms/narration-reference-ab.json, one job each, all with this 'text' and seed 1166: 'synthetic' clones asset:bench/narrator.wav (Audio8's own default voice, bench/workflows/narrator-reference-s6.json) with default sampling; 'human' clones asset:bench/narrator-human.wav (John Greenman's public-domain LibriVox reading, bench/workflows/narrator-human-librivox.json) with default sampling; 'sampling' clones the synthetic reference with 'generate_kwargs' raising temperature above the model's effective default (0.7, from its generation_config.json). An empty 'generate_kwargs' is the model's default sampling. Keep both reference assets before running the arms: a missing asset is refused at submit.

variables.text: Four score and seven years ago our fathers brought forth on this continent, a new nation, conceived in Liberty, and dedicated to the proposition that all men are created equal. Now we are engaged in a great civil war, testing whether that nation, or any nation so conceived and so dedicated, can long endure. We are met on a great battle-field of that war. We have come to dedicate a portion of that field, as a final resting place for those who here gave their lives that that nation might live. It is altogether fitting and proper that we should do this.
variables.reference_text: The tide comes in twice a day, and the lamp has to be ready for both.
